decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark (P1) — enter an address + optional title, it's stored and listed.” Round 1 client approved the proposed save feature.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, entering a URL to save a bookmark conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Page metadata | No auto-fetching titles/favicons/previews.” Round 2 maker repeated “no auto-fetched page titles/favicons.” Round 1 client only said “Those v1 assumptions are acceptable,” without stating the metadata expectation or difference.
decisions.note: The specification and plan explicitly omit automatic title, description, favicon, and preview collection. The generalized approval does not qualify as explicit acceptance of the reference difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed an optional manually entered title and later editing of “titles/addresses,” while also specifying “No auto-fetching titles.” Round 2 defined a bookmark as “web address + title + optional tags + timestamps.” The client approved without mentioning editable auto-collected title/description.
decisions.note: At the specification and planning gates, manual title handling partially overlaps the reference, but auto-collected title/description and description editing before and after saving are absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete (P2) — fix titles/addresses.” Round 2 maker: “A Bookmark = web address + title + optional tags + timestamps.” Round 1 and 2 clients approved without requesting description, note, or comprehensive tag editing.
decisions.note: The presented edit behavior and data model omit required editable fields, notably description and note.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “remove with confirmation.” Round 3 maker reported “delete behind a confirmation (cancel is safe),” and the round 3 client accepted deleting as working.
decisions.note: The recorded delete behavior conforms to the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker initially said only that the spec covered “duplicates.” Round 3 resolved the behavior as “duplicates warn but don't block.” Round 3 client accepted the version without mentioning duplicate prevention or editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Linked specification-to-implementation decision: merely warning while permitting duplicate creation conflicts with convergence to editing the existing bookmark. The earlier unspecified duplicate behavior is not counted separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered only “see the list” and explicitly excluded fetched favicons; round 2 limited stored bookmark data to address, title, tags, and timestamps. Round 3 reported a “List newest-first” without restoring descriptions or favicons. Clients approved without identifying the missing list content.
decisions.note: Across specification, plan, and implementation review, the presented list cannot expose the required description and fetched favicon per item.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “see the list, click to open in a new tab.” Round 3 maker confirmed “open in a new tab,” and the client accepted browsing as working.
decisions.note: Opening the selected bookmark's original URL in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included “tags,” and round 3 reported “Add a link with optional title + tags.” The clients approved tagging.
decisions.note: The presented save behavior supports assigning tags to a bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 1–3 mention tags, tag filtering, and optional tags, but never state whether existing tags are offered as autocomplete. The clients approve generally without addressing tag-entry suggestions.
decisions.note: The transcript does not establish either conformance or divergence for autocomplete during tag entry.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposed “tag filtering.” Round 3 maker reported “Tag filter,” and the client accepted tagging and searching as intended.
decisions.note: Filtering bookmarks by a selected tag conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reported “live text search,” but round 2 defined bookmark data as only address, title, tags, and timestamps, omitting description and note. The client accepted search without mentioning those missing searchable fields.
decisions.note: The data model makes full-text search over all required fields impossible; the presented search can at best cover a subset.

decisions.evidence: The maker described “text search” in round 1 and “live text search” in round 3, but never specified case sensitivity. The client did not ask or state an expectation about case handling.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive behavior cannot be established from the record.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 1 and 3 describe a separate tag filter and text search, but do not say whether `#tag` syntax is supported inside the search term. Client approvals do not address this distinction.
decisions.note: The presentation does not conclusively establish support for or exclusion of tag-query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 says tag filter and live text search are “combined with AND,” but does not describe AND/OR/NOT query operators, parentheses, or quoted literal operators. The client did not clarify or dispose of those semantics.
decisions.note: Combining two UI filters with AND is not evidence about the required Boolean query language, so divergence remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: The maker repeatedly described generic text search but never specified quoted exact-phrase matching. The client approved search generally without addressing phrases.
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase behavior cannot be established from the transcript.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presented the focused v1 stories as save, browse/open, edit/delete, and tags/search; round 3 said the implementation “exactly” matched that approved scope. Round 1 client called those features “sufficient for the first version,” and round 3 accepted without mentioning unread/read-later behavior.
decisions.note: The exhaustive v1 scope excludes the read-later state, separate unread view, and mark-read workflow. The client never states that difference or its expected behavior.

decisions.evidence: The round 1 story list and round 2 build slices contain no selection or bulk-action workflow, and round 3 says the delivered app exactly matches that narrow scope. Clients approve without mentioning multi-selection or whole-filter actions.
decisions.note: Bulk actions, including application to the current filtered collection, are excluded from the presented scope and pass without an expressed response.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker reports a fixed “List newest-first”; no presentation offers a user-selectable sort key. The final client accepts browsing without identifying the missing sorting control.
decisions.note: A fixed ordering does not satisfy the ability to choose among sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defines a bookmark as “web address + title + optional tags + timestamps,” with no note field; the round 3 delivered-story table also contains no notes or markdown rendering. Clients approve without mentioning notes.
decisions.note: Markdown note entry and rendered viewing are absent from the presented data model and scope.

decisions.evidence: The round 1 focused scope and round 2 implementation slices enumerate all v1 stories without local snapshots or PDF preservation; round 3 claims exact delivery of that scope. Clients call the scope sufficient and accept it without mentioning snapshots.
decisions.note: Local single-file HTML snapshots and the PDF-specific storage rule are excluded from the approved v1 presentation.

decisions.evidence: No Internet Archive action appears in the exhaustive round 1 scope, round 2 build slices, or round 3 delivered stories. Clients approve and accept without identifying this missing capability.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot creation is outside the presented v1 scope and passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents permanent removal with confirmation but no archive story; round 3 delivers delete only and says it exactly matches the approved scope. Clients accept without distinguishing reversible archive from permanent deletion or requesting an archive view.
decisions.note: The presented scope omits archiving, its distinction from deletion, and the separate archived list.

decisions.evidence: The round 1 organization scope contains only tags, tag filtering, and text search; round 3 delivers only “Tag filter + live text search.” Clients approve without mentioning saved filters or bundles.
decisions.note: Reusable bundles containing search terms and included/excluded tags are excluded from the presented scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly states “Import/export | Not included (no browser-bookmark import).” The client responds only “Those v1 assumptions are acceptable,” without independently stating the import/export expectation or difference.
decisions.note: Both Netscape HTML import and export are explicitly excluded. Referential approval of the maker's assumptions is insufficient for accepted_divergence under the rubric.

decisions.evidence: The exhaustive round 1 v1 stories, round 2 data model/build slices, and round 3 delivered-story table contain no personal display settings. Clients approve the focused scope and final version without mentioning settings.
decisions.note: Default sort, displayed-item, font-size, and related profile settings are outside the presented scope and pass without an expressed response.
